result:
Nothing in this repository works end to end yet: `src/ces_revisions/` is a greeting and two smoke tests. There is no spec, only the research brief and three research reports. So this goes through New-Project Entry. The literature review and gap analysis (brief Parts A and B) already exist in the three research files, so they are inputs, not outcomes. Every outcome below is a candidate from `specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md` (the brief), with costs and facts taken from the research files. Please confirm or strike each one.

## Outcomes (unranked)

| # | Outcome: what you get | From | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | Revision size over time for total nonfarm, separately for each of the four revision steps (1st→2nd, 2nd→3rd, 3rd→benchmark, post-benchmark/wedge-back), compared across eras (pre-2003, 2003–2019, 2020–22, after) | brief Part A; chatgpt §1.2 | Small data: total-nonfarm vintages are a few MB, and the FRED/ALFRED API allows 120 requests/min. NSA vintage coverage and the earliest usable vintage are measured by running it. |
| O2 | SA one- and two-month revisions split into an NSA-sample part and a seasonal-factor part, over time | brief Part C (seasonality); chatgpt exec summary ("no long-run published decomposition") | Needs matched NSA and SA vintages. Whether public archives cover both far enough back is measured by running it. |
| O3 | Whether collection interval (days from the 12th to first closing) and first-closing rate predict one-month revision dispersion | brief driver 2; claude exec summary | Collection days come from release calendars, arithmetic for about 500 months. The first-closing-rate series' earliest date is measured by running it. |
| O4 | Hand-built annual series: BLS real appropriations, CR/sequestration/shutdown events, BLS FTE, and CES sample size and mode mix | brief Part B (hand-built covariates) | Mostly your time: about 40 fiscal years of budget justifications plus FedScope pulls. Rough, only running it can tell. |
| O5 | A multi-vintage state-space model of total nonfarm: latent true path, news and noise per revision step, and the benchmark as an irregular high-precision observation with wedge-back, under constant variance | brief Part C | Compute is unknown without a fit; measured by running it. |
| O6 | Revision-scale estimates driven by covariates: stochastic volatility with covariates on the log scale, Student-t errors, horseshoe shrinkage, 2003 and 2020–22 breaks, and a written account of which effects are identified | brief Part C | Measured by running it. Expect it to cost more than O5. |
| O7 | O6 across NAICS supersectors with partial pooling of driver effects | brief Part C (hierarchy) | About 11× O6's data. Sampling cost is measured by running it. |

Qualities to place when the roadmap is written: manifests, traceability, full validation suites.

## Proposed tracks

- **A: Revision-size history (O1).** Known progression. It stands on its own as a descriptive answer.
- **B: Seasonal-factor vs. sample split (O2).** Research. Split from A and C because its answer stands without either one.
- **C: Collection interval (O3).** Research. Split from B because the two explain the same revisions, but each answer stands without the other.
- **D: Institutional covariates (O4).** Known progression. It is a data-building track that serves O6 and stands as descriptive context on its own.
- **E: Bayesian revision-scale model (O5–O7).** Research. Its method is open, and it draws on A's vintage panel and D's covariates.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14 managed with uv (`.python-version`, `uv.lock`).
- NumPyro (NUTS), Dynamax, Blackjax only if needed, ArviZ and Polars (brief, implementation notes).
- National CES all-employee estimates, in thousands of jobs (chatgpt scope line).

Proposed roadmap name: **`ces-revisions`**, written to `specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md`. No file with that name exists.

**One request:** please rank the outcomes within each track and the tracks among themselves. Also confirm or change the tracks, their kinds and the name, and strike any outcome you don't want.
